role.altitude: The Finance Director spends less time building and checking Excel packs and more time deciding. They own the finance control system: which jobs and model steps run, the thresholds that send items to a person, the logs the auditor reads, and who signs what.
reach: Learn how the FP&A Analyst builds the driver model, so the director can question forecast assumptions directly instead of waiting for the next version.
Learn how the Credit and Collections Officer records disputes and promises in AFAS, because the collection dashboard depends on that data being clean.
Learn the Controller's close checklist and SBR filing route, so the director knows which statutory steps sit outside AFAS.
skills_to_grow: Reading and testing data pipelines and their logs, not only the reports they produce
Writing decision rules and thresholds (credit limits, escalation, materiality) so code can apply them
AI governance in finance: approved tools, EU AI Act limits on credit scoring of sole traders, audit trail
Scenario thinking for fuel, interest, currency and flex labour cost
role.ambitious_version: A governed finance data platform reads AFAS, Rabobank CAMT.053 statements and the three agency portals every night. On top of it run a rolling 13-week cash and P&L forecast, a credit file per shipper and a collections dashboard. Small model steps draft the commentary. The director moves from a monthly view to a weekly forecast the business trusts, and closes faster because the board pack is built from the same numbers.

tasks.short: Analyse actuals, forecasts and cash to judge Noordhaven's current and future financial position for management and board.

steps.what: Pull AFAS ledger, AR/AP, agency hours and bank balances into Excel
Refresh driver model: volumes, shifts, flex hours, fuel, margins, cash
Find variances against budget and last forecast, explain the drivers

loop.input: variance table above materiality threshold plus AFAS journal descriptions and site cost-centre notes
loop.output: one-line driver explanation per variance with the source lines it used
loop.check: every number in the text is matched against the variance table by code; lines without a source are flagged
loop.stop: one pass per variance, max two retries; if the check fails the line shows 'unexplained' for the FP&A Analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: the drivers sit in free-text journal descriptions and notes that rules cannot read

steps.what: Judge outlook and scenarios: fuel, interest, flex labour, customer loss
Write financial position memo for management team and board

tasks.design: Replace the FP&A Excel workbook that ties AFAS, the agency portals and Rabobank with a nightly Python job on a governed data platform. It feeds a Power BI rolling forecast and variance dashboard. A bounded model step drafts variance explanations that code checks against the numbers, and a template builds the memo skeleton.
tasks.previous_blocker: The agency portals and bank files had no clean link to AFAS, so every refresh was manual Excel work. Building and keeping integrations was too slow for a 10-person team.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit has GetConnectors and Rabobank delivers CAMT.053. AI coding makes small pipelines cheap to build. Model steps can read journal text and draft explanations whose numbers code can check.
tasks.still_hard: Volume and customer assumptions come from operations and sales, and those do not sit in any system. Scenario judgement stays with people. Agency portal exports may change format without warning.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which risks matter, such as losing a large shipper, fuel spikes or CAO wage steps, and standing behind the outlook in front of the board and the bank.

ambition.what: A weekly re-forecast of P&L and 13-week cash, not a monthly one, with the director signing off a short outlook each Monday.

tasks.altitude: The director spends Monday reviewing a pre-built forecast and its explanations instead of chasing the workbook. They decide which drivers and thresholds the model uses.

reach.task: Maintaining the driver model and assumptions
reach.learn: How volume, shift and flex-hour drivers are built, so the director can test them directly.
Which accruals arrive late, because they limit how early the forecast can be trusted.

evidence.claim: Executive reporting takes about 32 hours a month, and AI-mature teams spend more on it, not less.
Data quality is the top barrier to finance AI (40.4%).
AFAS Profit exposes data via GetConnectors and Rabobank supports CAMT.053 statements.

assumptions: FP&A owns a driver-based Excel model today.
Power BI already reads a nightly AFAS extract and can be extended.
unknowns: Do the three agency portals offer an API or only CSV/PDF exports?
Is there a data platform under IT governance, or does Power BI hold the only copy?
Which operational volume data (WMS, TMS) is available, and from which system?
research_questions: Can FP&A explain 80% of monthly variances from journal text and cost-centre data alone?
Does a weekly re-forecast change any decision the management team takes?
How many hours a month does FP&A spend on the data pull today?

tasks.short: Assess credit limit requests for new and growing shippers, and prepare bank facility applications and covenant files.

steps.what: Receive credit limit request from sales or collections by mail
Gather KvK extract, credit report, annual accounts, AFAS payment history
Analyse figures and draft limit proposal with terms

loop.input: filed annual accounts PDF and credit report of a legal entity
loop.output: key ratios (equity, current ratio, result) and red flags in a fixed form, with page references
loop.check: extracted totals must balance (assets = liabilities plus equity); mismatches send the file to manual entry
loop.stop: one extraction plus one retry; then manual. Sole traders (natural persons) skip the model and use rules only, to stay out of EU AI Act Annex III 5(b)
loop.why_not_simpler: filed accounts arrive as PDFs in varying layouts; the limit itself is computed by deterministic rules from the extracted ratios

steps.what: Decide limit, payment terms and any security
Record limit in AFAS and inform sales and customer

tasks.design: A request form in Teams/SharePoint starts a workflow that pulls the KvK extract, credit report and AFAS payment history into one credit file. Deterministic rules from the written credit policy compute a proposed limit. For legal entities a bounded model step extracts ratios from the filed accounts. The director approves in one screen, and the approved limit is written to the AFAS debtor record with a log entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Credit data sat in PDFs, agency portals and AFAS screens, and the credit policy was mostly in the director's head. Too few requests came in to justify a credit tool.
tasks.enabler_now: KvK and credit agencies offer APIs, AFAS UpdateConnectors can set debtor limits, and model steps can read filed accounts PDFs with checks that the totals balance.
tasks.still_hard: Writing the credit policy as explicit rules. Sole-trader hauliers are natural persons, so model scoring would be high-risk under the EU AI Act and stays out. Small shippers rarely file useful accounts.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing commercial value against risk for a shipper, and agreeing security or shorter terms in a conversation with sales and the customer.

ambition.what: Review every shipper's credit limit each quarter against payment behaviour, not only when a new request arrives.

tasks.altitude: The director approves a prepared file in minutes instead of building it. They own the written credit policy and its thresholds, including which requests below a set amount the Collections Officer may approve alone.

reach.learn: Which payment patterns come before a default, so they can be written into the limit rules.
How limits and provisions connect at month end.

evidence.claim: Creditworthiness scoring of natural persons is high-risk under the EU AI Act.
A large company may not agree more than 30 days of payment terms with a small supplier.
Advisors say credit and cash allocation decisions need mandatory human approval with timestamped logs.
KvK and Dutch credit agencies offer data APIs.

assumptions: 'Loan applications' here means shipper credit limit requests and the bank facility file.
There are a few to tens of requests a week.
unknowns: Is there a written credit policy, and who may approve which amounts?
Which credit agency does Noordhaven subscribe to, and does the contract include API access?
How many shipper customers are sole traders?
research_questions: What share of credit requests could rules decide without changing the outcome the director would choose?
How often do filed accounts PDFs extract cleanly with balancing totals?
Have past bad debts shown early signals in AFAS payment history?

tasks.short: Review aging and collection reports to see overdue balances, DSO and which debtors need action.

steps.what: Export aging list from AFAS and format in Excel
Add dispute, promise-to-pay and contact status from mail and notes

loop.input: debtor emails in the shared collections mailbox linked to an AFAS debtor number
loop.output: status label (dispute, promise with date, no response, paid claim) with quoted sentence
loop.check: label must be from the fixed list and the date must parse; the Collections Officer confirms before it is stored in AFAS
loop.stop: one pass per mail; unclear mails are labelled 'needs reading'
loop.why_not_simpler: debtor replies are free text in Dutch and English

steps.what: Review top overdue debtors, DSO trend and site splits
Weekly talk with collections and controller on actions
Decide escalations: credit stop, legal, provision

tasks.design: Replace the weekly Excel aging pack with a Power BI collections page on the nightly AFAS extract, showing DSO, overdue by debtor and site, and dispute status. A bounded model step labels debtor mails in the shared collections mailbox, and the officer confirms the label before it goes into AFAS. A notification flags debtors that cross a set threshold to the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dispute and promise information lived in Outlook, not in AFAS, so the report needed manual notes every week.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI already runs on AFAS data. Model steps can label Dutch and English mails reliably enough for a person to confirm with one click.
tasks.still_hard: Disputes often start in operations (damaged goods, waiting time) and reach finance late. The 30-day cap on payment terms for small suppliers applies on the payables side and needs its own check.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing when to stop deliveries to a large shipper and having that conversation with sales and the customer.

ambition.what: A forward cash-in forecast per week for the next 30 to 60 days, built from promises and payment patterns, instead of explaining DSO after the fact.

tasks.altitude: The director reads a live dashboard and only acts on flagged debtors. They set the escalation thresholds and decide the credit stops.

reach.learn: How disputes are recorded, so the labels match how the work is done.
Which invoice errors cause disputes, so they can be fixed at the source.

evidence.claim: 81% of Dutch finance professionals explain DSO after the fact; only 12% plan cash-in more than 30 days ahead.
Power BI can show aging and DSO from an AFAS extract.

assumptions: The AFAS extract includes open items with due dates.
unknowns: Are disputes recorded anywhere in AFAS today?
Does the works council need to agree to reading the shared mailbox with a model? Personal data of debtor contacts is processed under the AVG.
research_questions: What share of overdue amounts is caused by disputes rather than slow payment?
Does a mail label reach 90% agreement with the Collections Officer on a month of mail?
Would a weekly cash-in forecast change bank facility usage?

tasks.short: Prepare the board pack, annual accounts, bank covenant and statutory reports, then sign off and file them.

steps.what: Extract trial balance and closing data from AFAS
Build board pack, covenant calculation and accounts tables in Excel/Word
Write commentary and notes to the figures

loop.input: report tables, prior period commentary and variance notes
loop.check: code compares every figure and percentage in the text with the tables; mismatches block the draft
loop.stop: two attempts per section, then the section stays empty for the director
loop.why_not_simpler: the commentary is prose that changes each period; templates only cover the fixed parts

steps.what: Answer auditor and board questions, settle disclosures
Sign off and file: KVK via SBR, bank, CBS

tasks.design: A scheduled job reads the closed AFAS period into a reporting dataset and fills fixed templates for the board pack, the bank covenant calculation and the accounts tables, with a reconciliation check against the trial balance. A bounded model step drafts commentary whose numbers code checks. Filing to KVK goes through a separate SBR tool because AFAS cannot file for large companies, and every external submission needs the director's sign-off.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report layouts changed every period and were rebuilt by hand in Excel and Word. Statutory formats such as SBR need tooling outside AFAS.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes template generators and reconciliation checks cheap to build and change. Model steps can draft commentary that code checks figure by figure.
tasks.still_hard: Disclosure judgement, auditor negotiation and new rules: CSRD applies only above 1,000 employees and €450 million turnover, and Dutch B2B e-invoicing reporting is coming from 2030–2031. Report volume tends to grow once reports are cheap to make.
tasks.human_edge: Signing the accounts and the covenant statement, judging disclosures with the auditor, and explaining the results to the board and the bank.
tasks.altitude: The director reviews a ready pack and writes only the key messages. They decide which reports exist and cap their number so the time saved is not spent on more reports.

reach.learn: Which audit adjustments recur, so checks can catch them before the pack is built.
The mapping from AFAS accounts to report lines, which the generator will own.

evidence.claim: Large companies file accounts with KVK via SBR from FY2025, and AFAS cannot do this for them.
CSRD now applies above 1,000 employees and €450 million turnover.
B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and digital reporting from 1 July 2031 are planned.
Workday's Accounting Agent prepares entries and leaves review and judgement with the team.
More AI-mature teams spend more hours on executive reporting.

assumptions: Noordhaven is a large company under Dutch law (BW 2:397) and files through SBR.
There is a bank facility with financial covenants reported each quarter.
unknowns: Turnover, which decides whether CSRD applies.
Which SBR filing tool or accountant files the accounts today?
Does the auditor accept generated tables with a reconciliation log as audit evidence?
research_questions: How many hours a quarter go into rebuilding the board pack layout?
Can the AFAS-to-report-line mapping stay stable across a full year?
Does the auditor's adjustment count fall after the generator and checks are in place?
